questions.solution:
The seed habit is considered an important step in plant evolution. Its precursor is seen in heterosporous pteridophytes (like Selaginella and Salvinia) where the female gametophyte is retained on the parent sporophyte for variable periods.

The female gametophyte does not have an independent free-living existence; it is permanently retained within the megasporangium (ovule) on the parent sporophyte. Fertilization and the subsequent development of the zygote into an embryo occur within this retained structure, which eventually transforms into a seed.

The formation of cones, leaf adaptations, and wind pollination are characteristic features of many gymnosperms but are not the direct morphological cause of the seed habit.

Answer: The retention of the female gametophyte within the megasporangium on the parent sporophyte
